source_text: Duobus ergo his ostendi dicit Deum non posse mentiri, hoc ipso, quia promisit atque id, quod promisit, quia se testatur implere. Non quod Deus sine attestatione tali imbecillum atque dubium soleat habere sermonem, sed ut veritatem suam documentis grandibus oneraret, eo genere elocutionis abusus est, quod hominibus etiam fallere solitis credi faciat. Hoc ergo pondere in praesenti quoque causa admonet Deus atque praescribit, ut et nullus hoc, quod Traduciani asserunt, de populo suspicetur et Deum non posse eo quem detestatur modo iudicare cognoscat: Vivo ego, dicit Adonai Dominus, si amplius dicetur parabola haec in Israel [n53] .
pass_a_gloss: By these two therefore he says it is shown that God cannot lie, by this very thing, because he promised and because he testifies that he fulfills that which he promised. Not that God without such attestation is accustomed to have a weak and doubtful speech, but that he might load his truth with great documents he used that kind of elocution which makes even humans accustomed to deceive be believed. With this weight therefore in the present cause also God admonishes and prescribes, that both no one from the people suspect this which the advocates of inherited sin assert, and that he know that God cannot judge in that mode which he detests: I live, says Adonai the Lord, if this parable shall still be said in Israel.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent

pass_b_english: He therefore says that these two things show God cannot lie: the fact that he promised, and the fact that he calls himself to witness that he will fulfill his promise. This does not mean that God’s word is normally weak or doubtful without such an attestation. Rather, to load his truth with weighty proofs, he adopted the kind of speech that makes even people accustomed to deceiving others believable. With this same weight God warns and commands in the present case: no one among his people should suspect what the advocates of inherited sin assert, and everyone should understand that God cannot judge in the way he condemns. ‘As I live, says the Lord God, this proverb shall no longer be spoken in Israel’ (Ezekiel 18:3).

choices.why: Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
